ca-cdtfa.notes: Free: Pub 107 says "There is no charge for a seller's permit" but CDTFA "may ask you for a security deposit" depending on business type and expected taxable sales. Pub 107 also says applicants need bank account details and estimated income. Temporary permits are valid up to 90 days. The online questions themselves sit behind the eServ flow; fields above are CDTFA's published 'information needed' list, not the screen-by-screen questions. No mailing address published for seller's permit applications (in person at any CDTFA office is the alternative).

ca-llc-5.notes: Fee $70.00 (forms page and printed on form; plus optional copy fees $1 first page/$0.50 each attachment page and $5 certification). Online 5 days or less vs PDF 10+ days. Paper PDF linked at https://bpd.cdn.sos.ca.gov/llc/forms/llc-5.pdf but I could not open it, so the revision shown (REV 11/2020) comes from a filed image and may be stale; the bizfile online screens may word items differently. Computer-generated/font signatures are NOT accepted on paper filings. No filing mailing address confirmed (forms page only says forms 'can be submitted by mail or in person' and points to the contact page). Form warns registered LLCs may owe the $800 FTB annual tax.

destination.evidence: "If paying by Web Pay, do not file form FTB 3522." The voucher has no signature line.

ca-ftb-3522.notes: Payment voucher, not an application. $800 due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the taxable year (April 15, 2026 for calendar-year LLCs); next business day if weekend/holiday. Paying online via Web Pay (free, bank account) or credit card replaces the voucher: 'If no payment is due or paid electronically, do not mail this voucher.' FTB notes 'some recently registered business entities may not be able to use the FTB Web Pay application'. Library URL https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/ was not opened; Web Pay host taken from an official search result (webapp.ftb.ca.gov/WebPay). For taxable year 2027 the library will need the 2027 voucher.
